results.title: Polynomial decay implies $L^p$ membership
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a normed additive commutative group and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable. Suppose there are real numbers $C \ge 0$ and $q > 1$ such that $\|f(x)\| \le C (1 + |x|)^{-q}$ for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R})$, with respect to Lebesgue measure, for every $p \in [1, \infty]$.

results.title: Pointwise polynomial decay implies $L^p$ membership

results.summary: For a natural number $n$, real numbers $t_0, t_1, \dots, t_n$ form a partition of $[0, 1]$ when $0 = t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_n = 1$.

results.title: The integer line graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The integer line is the simple graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ in which $m$ and $n$ are adjacent exactly when $|m - n| = 1$.

results.title: The product graph $G \times \mathbb{Z}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on $V$, the graph $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ is the box product of $G$ with the integer line: its vertex set is $V \times \mathbb{Z}$, and $(v, m)$ and $(w, n)$ are adjacent exactly when either $v$ and $w$ are adjacent in $G$ and $m = n$, or $v = w$ and $|m - n| = 1$.

results.title: Open subgraph of the product graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$, let $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ denote the box product of $G$ with the integer line, and let $\omega$ assign true or false to every unordered pair of points of $V \times \mathbb{Z}$. The open subgraph of $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ determined by $\omega$ is the simple graph on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ in which $a$ and $b$ are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ and…

results.title: Open cluster in the product graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$, let $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ denote the box product of $G$ with the integer line, let $\omega$ assign true or false to every unordered pair of points of $V \times \mathbb{Z}$, and let $x \in V \times \mathbb{Z}$. The open cluster of $x$ is the set of points $y \in V \times \mathbb{Z}$ that are reachable from $x$ (including $x$ itself) in the open subgraph of $G \times \mathbb{Z}$…

results.title: Bernoulli bond law on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $V$ and $0 \le p \le 1$, the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ is the product measure on configurations $\omega$, which assign true (open) or false (closed) to every unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ of points of $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ (with $a = b$ allowed), under which the values $\omega(e)$ are independent and each is true with probability $p$ and false with probability $1 - p$.

results.title: Almost-sure properties under the Bernoulli bond law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $V$ be a type, let $p$ be a real number with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $P$ be a property of configurations $\omega$, that is, of functions assigning true or false to every unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ of points of $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ (with $a = b$ allowed). We say that $P$ holds almost surely if $P(\omega)$ holds for almost every $\omega$ with respect to the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Open subgraph of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$ and let $\omega$ assign true or false to every unordered pair of elements of $V$. The open subgraph of $G$ determined by $\omega$ is the simple graph on $V$ in which $a$ and $b$ are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in $G$ and $\omega(\{a, b\})$ is true.

results.title: Open cluster in a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$, let $\omega$ assign true or false to every unordered pair of elements of $V$, and let $x \in V$. The open cluster of $x$ is the set of vertices $y \in V$ that are reachable from $x$ (including $x$ itself) in the open subgraph of $G$ determined by $\omega$, that is, joined to $x$ by a path whose edges $e$ are edges of $G$ with $\omega(e)$ true.

results.title: Bernoulli bond law on $V$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $V$ and $0 \le p \le 1$, the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V$ is the product measure on configurations $\omega$, which assign true (open) or false (closed) to every unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ of elements of $V$ (with $a = b$ allowed), under which the values $\omega(e)$ are independent and each is true with probability $p$ and false with probability $1 - p$.

results.title: Critical probability for bond percolation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a countable vertex set $V$, the critical probability $p_c(G)$ is the infimum of the set consisting of $1$ together with every $p \in [0, 1]$ for which, under the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V$, the event that the open cluster in $G$ of some vertex is infinite has positive probability. In particular $p_c(G) = 1$ when no such $p$ exists.

results.title: Degeneracy on a vertex set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $U \subseteq V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $U$ if every nonempty subset $W \subseteq U$ contains a vertex $v$ with at most $k$ neighbors in $W$.

results.title: Degenerate graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex type $V$ is $k$-degenerate, for a natural number $k$, if it is $k$-degenerate on the full vertex set $V$: every nonempty set $W$ of vertices contains a vertex with at most $k$ neighbors in $W$.

results.title: Degeneracy on a vertex set is monotone in the degree bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $U \subseteq V$, and let $k \le l$ be natural numbers. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $U$, then $G$ is $l$-degenerate on $U$.

results.title: Degeneracy on a vertex set passes to subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $T \subseteq U \subseteq V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $U$, then $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $T$.

results.title: A degenerate graph is degenerate on every vertex set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate, then $G$ is $k$-degenerate on every subset $U \subseteq V$.

results.title: A degenerate vertex set has a vertex of small degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $s \subseteq V$ be nonempty. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $s$, then some vertex $v \in s$ has at most $k$ neighbors in $s$.

results.title: The edgeless graph is degenerate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the edgeless graph on a finite vertex set is $k$-degenerate.

results.title: Degeneracy is monotone in the bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate and $k \le l$, then $G$ is $l$-degenerate.

results.title: Bounded maximum degree implies degeneracy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set. If every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $k$, then $G$ is $k$-degenerate.

results.title: Degeneracy ordering
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. A map $e : V \to \mathbb{N}$ is a degeneracy ordering of $G$ with bound $k$ if $e$ is injective and every vertex $v$ has at most $k$ neighbors $w$ with $e(v) < e(w)$.

results.title: Degeneracy orderings of a vertex set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $s \subseteq V$. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $s$, then there is a map $e : V \to \mathbb{N}$, injective on $s$, such that every $v \in s$ has at most $k$ neighbors $w \in s$ with $e(v) < e(w)$.

results.title: Degenerate graphs have degeneracy orderings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $G$ is a $k$-degenerate simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, then $G$ has a degeneracy ordering with bound $k$: an injective map $e : V \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every vertex $v$ has at most $k$ neighbors $w$ with $e(v) < e(w)$.

results.title: Coloring a $k$-degenerate vertex set with $k + 1$ colors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $s \subseteq V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $s$, then there is a map $f : V \to \{0, 1, \dots, k\}$ such that $f(a) \ne f(b)$ for all adjacent vertices $a, b \in s$.

results.title: $k$-degenerate graphs are $(k + 1)$-colorable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. Every $k$-degenerate simple graph on a finite vertex set is $(k + 1)$-colorable.

results.title: Chromatic number of a degenerate graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is a $k$-degenerate simple graph on a finite vertex set, then the chromatic number of $G$ is at most $k + 1$.

results.title: Well-formed Akari boards
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An Akari board is well formed when every entry is at most $6$ and all its rows have the same length.

results.title: Feasible Akari boards

results.title: The Akari decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Akari (Light Up) decision problem accepts a list of booleans $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of lists of lists of natural numbers, to an Akari board that is well formed and feasible; it rejects every list that does not decode.

results.title: AKARI (LIGHT UP) is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Akari decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.title: Partition function of a chain CRF
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a chain conditional random field with a finite set of states and weights in a semiring, and an observation stream $x$, the partition function at time $t$ is $Z_t = \sum_z w_t(z)$, the total weight of all label paths $z$ of length $t + 1$, where $w_t(z)$ is the unnormalized weight of $z$ given $x$.

results.title: Forward variables of a chain CRF
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a chain conditional random field with a finite set of states, weights in a semiring, unary potentials $u_t(s)$ and transition potentials $\tau_t(s', s)$ given the observation stream $x$, the forward variables are defined by $\alpha_0(s) = u_0(s)$ and $\alpha_{t+1}(s) = \left(\sum_{s'} \alpha_t(s')\, \tau_t(s', s)\right) u_{t+1}(s)$, the sum running over all states $s'$.

results.title: Path weights of a chain CRF are bounded by the Viterbi variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a chain conditional random field with a nonempty finite set of states, weights in a linearly ordered commutative semiring, and an observation stream $x$, for every $t$ and every label path $z = (z_0, \dots, z_t)$, the weight of $z$ is at most the Viterbi variable at time $t$ of its last state $z_t$.

results.title: The Viterbi variables of a chain CRF are attained

results.title: The chain CRF of a hidden Markov model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $h$ be a hidden Markov model with initial weights $\pi(s)$, transition weights $a(s, s')$ and emission weights $b(s, o)$ in a linearly ordered commutative semiring, all nonnegative. Its chain CRF has, for every observation stream $x$, unary potentials $u_0(s) = \pi(s)\, b(s, x_0)$ and $u_t(s) = b(s, x_t)$ for $t \ge 1$, and transition potentials $\tau_t(s, s') = a(s, s')$ at every step $t$.

results.title: The chain CRF of a hidden Markov model has the same path weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $h$ be a hidden Markov model with nonnegative weights in a linearly ordered commutative semiring, and let $x$ be an observation stream. For every $t$ and every state path $z = (z_0, \dots, z_t)$, the weight of $z$ in the chain CRF of $h$ given $x$ equals the joint weight in $h$ of the state path $z$ and the observations $x_0, \dots, x_t$.

results.title: The Viterbi path of a chain CRF
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $c$ be a chain CRF with states $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, where $n \ge 1$, and weights in a linearly ordered commutative semiring, and let $x$ be an observation sequence. For $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the Viterbi path of length $t + 1$ is the backtracked path ending in the first state, in the order $0, \dots, n-1$, that maximizes the Viterbi table at time $t$.

results.title: The Viterbi path of a chain CRF has maximal weight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a chain conditional random field with states $0, \dots, n - 1$ where $n \ge 1$, weights in a linearly ordered commutative semiring, and an observation stream $x$, for every $t$ and every label path $z$ of length $t + 1$, the weight of $z$ is at most the weight of Viterbi's MAP path of length $t + 1$.

results.title: Gaussian belief
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For an index type $n$, a belief about the state consists of a mean $m \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and a covariance matrix $P$, an arbitrary real $n \times n$ matrix. It describes the Gaussian distribution $N(m, P)$ when $P$ is positive semidefinite (the belief is valid); for other matrices Mathlib's multivariate Gaussian is a junk value. Prediction with positive semidefinite process noise, update with positive definite…

results.title: Valid Gaussian beliefs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A belief is valid when its covariance matrix is positive semidefinite.

results.title: Law of a belief
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The law of a belief with mean $m$ and covariance $P$ is Mathlib's multivariate Gaussian measure $N(m, P)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. It is the Gaussian distribution with mean $m$ and covariance $P$ when $P$ is positive semidefinite (the belief is valid); otherwise it is the point mass at $m$.

results.title: Kalman prediction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given real $n \times n$ matrices $F$ and $Q$, the prediction of a belief with mean $m$ and covariance $P$ is the belief with mean $F m$ and covariance $F P F^\top + Q$. It models the dynamics $x' = F x + w$ with process noise $w \sim N(0, Q)$.

results.title: Kalman gain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real $p \times n$ matrix $H$, a real $p \times p$ matrix $R$ and a belief with covariance $P$, the Kalman gain is the real $n \times p$ matrix $K = P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1}$, where the inverse is taken to be $0$ when $H P H^\top + R$ is singular.

results.title: Kalman filter update
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a real $p \times n$ observation matrix $H$, a real $p \times p$ matrix $R$, an observation $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a belief with mean $m$ and covariance $P$, the updated belief has mean $m + K (y - H m)$ and covariance $(I - K H) P$, where $K = P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1}$ is the Kalman gain and the matrix inverse is taken to be $0$ when $H P H^\top + R$ is singular.

results.title: Kalman filter step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given real $n \times n$ matrices $F$ and $Q$, a real $p \times n$ matrix $H$, a real $p \times p$ matrix $R$ and an observation $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$, one filter step sends a belief to the update, with $H$, $R$ and $y$, of its prediction with $F$ and $Q$.

results.title: Prediction preserves validity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ and $Q$ be real $n \times n$ matrices with $Q$ positive semidefinite. If a belief is valid, that is, its covariance $P$ is positive semidefinite, then the predicted belief, with covariance $F P F^\top + Q$, is valid.

results.title: Schur form of the updated covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix, $R$ a real $p \times p$ matrix and $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$, and let a belief have covariance $P$. Then the covariance of the belief updated with $H$, $R$ and $y$ equals $P - P H^\top (H P H^\top + R)^{-1} H P$. Here $M^{-1}$ is the matrix inverse, taken to be $0$ when $M$ is singular, so no invertibility is assumed.

results.title: The Kalman update preserves validity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix, $R$ a symmetric positive definite real $p \times p$ matrix and $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$. If a belief is valid, then the belief updated with $H$, $R$ and $y$ is valid.

results.title: A filter step preserves validity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ and $Q$ be real $n \times n$ matrices with $Q$ positive semidefinite, $H$ a real $p \times n$ matrix, $R$ a positive definite real $p \times p$ matrix and $y \in \mathbb{R}^p$. If a belief is valid (its covariance is positive semidefinite), then so is the belief obtained from it by one filter step with $F$, $Q$, $H$, $R$ and the observation $y$.

results.title: The predict step is exact
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $w$ be measurable, independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ on a probability space. If $x$ has the law $N(m, P)$ of a belief with mean $m$ and positive semidefinite covariance $P$, and $w$ has law $N(0, Q)$ with $Q$ positive semidefinite, then for every real $n \times n$ matrix $F$ the random vector $F x + w$ has the law of the predicted belief, $N(F m, F P F^\top + Q)$.

results.title: The update step is the exact posterior
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v$ a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^p$ on a probability space, with $x$ independent of $v$. Suppose $x$ has the law $N(m, P)$ of a belief with mean $m$ and positive semidefinite covariance $P$, and $v$ has law $N(0, R)$ with $R$ positive semidefinite. Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix with $H P H^\top + R$ invertible, and put $Y = H x + v$.…

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $w$ be measurable random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $v$ a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^p$ on a probability space, with $x$ independent of $w$ and the pair $(x, w)$ independent of $v$. Suppose $x$ has the law $N(m, P)$ of a belief with mean $m$ and positive semidefinite covariance $P$, $w$ has law $N(0, Q)$ and $v$ has law $N(0, R)$, with $Q$ and $R$ positive semidefinite. part.title: Bitonic sorter
api: Running a comparator network on natural-number-indexed wires
Restricting comparators to finitely many wires
Extension of a Boolean vector by false

uses: Sorting networks and the zero-one principle

results.title: Comparator on natural-number-indexed wires
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. For wires $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ and an assignment $f$ of values in $\alpha$ to the wires $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the comparator $(i, j)$ applied to $f$ puts $\min(f(i), f(j))$ on wire $i$, puts $\max(f(i), f(j))$ on wire $j$ when $j \ne i$, and leaves every other wire unchanged.

results.title: Running a comparator network on natural-number-indexed wires
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order. Given a list $ps$ of comparators, each a pair $(i, j)$ of natural numbers, and an input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ giving the value on each wire, running $ps$ on $f$ applies the comparators of $ps$ to the wire values one after another, from first to last. The comparator $(i, j)$ puts the minimum of the values on wires $i$ and $j$ on wire $i$ and their maximum on wire $j$, and leaves…

results.title: Comparators within an interval
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list $ps$ of comparators, each a pair $(i, j)$ of natural numbers, lies within $[l, h)$ if every comparator $(i, j)$ in $ps$ satisfies $l \le i < h$ and $l \le j < h$.

results.title: Locality of comparator networks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order and let $ps$ be a list of comparators $(i, j)$ on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires that all lie within $[l, h)$, that is, $l \le i < h$ and $l \le j < h$ for every $(i, j)$ in $ps$. Then for every input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ and every wire $x$ with $x < l$ or $h \le x$, the value of wire $x$ after running $ps$ on $f$ is $f(x)$.

results.title: Constant blocks stay constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order, let $l, h \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $c$ be a list of comparators on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires each of which joins two wires $x$ with $l \le x < h$. If an input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ takes the same value $a$ on every wire $x$ with $l \le x < h$, then running $c$ on $f$ gives an output that also takes the value $a$ on every such wire.

results.title: Half-cleaner
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $b$, the half-cleaner on the block of wires $[b, b + 2m)$ is the list of comparators $(b + i, b + m + i)$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots, m - 1$, in this order: it compares wire $b + i$ with wire $b + m + i$.

results.title: Output of the half-cleaner
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linear order, let $m, b \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be an input on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires. Running the half-cleaner on $[b, b + 2m)$ on $f$ puts $\min(f(b + i), f(b + m + i))$ on wire $b + i$ and $\max(f(b + i), f(b + m + i))$ on wire $b + m + i$ for every $i < m$, and leaves the value $f(x)$ on every wire $x$ outside $[b, b + 2m)$ unchanged.

results.title: Interval indicators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ is an interval indicator of length $L$ if there are natural numbers $a \le e \le L$ such that for every $i < L$, $s(i) = 1$ exactly when $a \le i < e$.

results.title: Bitonic 0-1 sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $s : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ is bitonic of length $L$ if either $s$ or its complement $1 - s$ is an interval indicator of length $L$; that is, on the positions $0, \dots, L - 1$ it has the form $0^a 1^b 0^c$ or $1^a 0^b 1^c$. Values of $s$ at positions $i \ge L$ are unconstrained.

results.title: The half-cleaner lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_{2m-1}$ be a bitonic sequence of Booleans, ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$. For $i < m$ put $\ell_i = \min(s_i, s_{i+m})$ and $u_i = \max(s_i, s_{i+m})$. Then either $\ell_i = \mathrm{false}$ for every $i < m$ and $u_0, \dots, u_{m-1}$ is bitonic, or $u_i = \mathrm{true}$ for every $i < m$ and $\ell_0, \dots, \ell_{m-1}$ is bitonic.

results.title: Sorted on a block
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A Boolean sequence $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is sorted on the block $[b, b + L)$ if $g(b + i) \le g(b + j)$ for all $i \le j < L$, where Booleans are ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$.

results.title: Bitonic merger
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bitonic merger on the block of wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ is the list of comparators defined by recursion on $k$. For $k = 0$ it is empty. On the block $[b, b + 2^{k+1})$ it is the half-cleaner on $[b, b + 2^{k+1})$, followed by the bitonic merger on $[b, b + 2^k)$, followed by the bitonic merger on $[b + 2^k, b + 2^{k+1})$.

results.title: The bitonic merger sorts every bitonic `0`-`1` input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire $x \in \mathbb{N}$, with Booleans ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$. If the sequence $f(b), f(b + 1), \dots, f(b + 2^k - 1)$ is bitonic, then running the bitonic merger on the block $[b, b + 2^k)$ on $f$ gives an assignment $g$ that is sorted on that block: $g(b + i) \le g(b + j)$ whenever $i \le j < 2^k$.

results.title: Reversing the comparators conjugates the network by complement on Booleans
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $ps$ be a list of comparators on $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires and let $ps'$ be obtained by replacing each comparator $(i, j)$ in $ps$ by $(j, i)$. For every input $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ and every wire $x$, the value of wire $x$ after running $ps'$ on $f$ is the negation of the value of wire $x$ after running $ps$ on the complemented input $y \mapsto \lnot f(y)$.

results.title: Batcher's bitonic sorter on a block of wires
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A comparator $(i, j)$ puts the minimum of the values on wires $i$ and $j$ on wire $i$ and the maximum on wire $j$. Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block of wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ is the list of comparators defined by recursion on $k$. For $k = 0$ it is empty. On the block $[b, b + 2^{k+1})$ it is Batcher's bitonic sorter on $[b, b + 2^k)$, followed by Batcher's bitonic sorter on $[b + 2^k, b + 2^{k+1})$ with every…

results.title: The bitonic sorter sorts every `0`-`1` input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f$ assign a Boolean value to each wire $x \in \mathbb{N}$, with Booleans ordered by $\mathrm{false} < \mathrm{true}$. Running Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block $[b, b + 2^k)$ on $f$ gives an assignment $g$ that is sorted on that block: $g(b + i) \le g(b + j)$ whenever $i \le j < 2^k$.

results.title: Size of the half-cleaner
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $b$, the half-cleaner on the block of wires $[b, b + 2m)$ has exactly $m$ comparators.

results.title: Size of the bitonic merger
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $b$, the bitonic merger on the block of wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ has $k \cdot 2^{k-1}$ comparators; precisely, twice its number of comparators equals $k \cdot 2^k$.

results.title: Size of the bitonic sorter on a block of wires
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $b$, the bitonic sorter on the block of $\mathbb{N}$-indexed wires $[b, b + 2^k)$ has $k(k+1)2^k/4$ comparators; precisely, four times its number of comparators equals $k(k+1)2^k$.

results.title: Restricting comparators to finitely many wires
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $N$ and a list of comparators on wires indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, this is the network on the $N$ wires $0, \dots, N - 1$ that keeps, in their original order, the comparators $(i, j)$ with $i < N$ and $j < N$, and drops all the others.

results.title: Extension of a Boolean vector by false
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean vector $v = (v_0, \dots, v_{N-1})$, its extension by $\mathrm{false}$ is the function on $\mathbb{N}$ that takes the value $v_j$ at each $j < N$ and the value $\mathrm{false}$ at each $j \ge N$.

results.title: Transported comparator lists agree with the original on Boolean inputs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $P$ be a list of comparators on natural-number-indexed wires, each of which joins two wires below $N$. For every Boolean input $v$ on the wires $0, \dots, N - 1$, run the network on $N$ wires obtained from $P$ on $v$ and extend its output by $\mathrm{false}$ to all wires in $\mathbb{N}$; the result equals the result of running $P$ on the extension of $v$ by $\mathrm{false}$.

results.title: Batcher's bitonic sorting network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires is the comparator network on the wires $0, 1, \dots, 2^k - 1$ made of the comparators of Batcher's bitonic sorter on the block $[0, 2^k)$ that join two wires below $2^k$ (in fact all of them), applied in the same order.

results.title: Batcher's bitonic sorter sorts every input over every linear order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every linearly ordered type $\alpha$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires sorts inputs over $\alpha$: for every assignment $v$ of elements of $\alpha$ to the wires $0, 1, \dots, 2^k - 1$, the output of the network on $v$ is monotone in the wire order.

results.title: Comparator count of Batcher's bitonic sorter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, Batcher's bitonic sorting network on $2^k$ wires has $k(k+1)2^k/4$ comparators; precisely, four times its number of comparators equals $k(k+1)2^k$.

results.title: Uniform bound on the expected site-frequency spectrum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The expected number of sites with `i` derived copies in a sample of `n`, `1 ≤ i < n`, is bounded uniformly in the selection coefficient: `|E ξ_i(σ)| ≤ |θ| C(n, i)`.

results.title: Site-frequency spectrum under a distribution of fitness effects
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected unfolded site-frequency spectrum under the distribution of fitness effects `μ` (a law on the scaled selection coefficient `σ = 2Ns`): `∫ E ξ_i(σ) dμ(σ)`, where each new mutation draws its own `σ` from `μ`.

results.title: Frequency density averaged over a distribution of fitness effects
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Poisson-random-field frequency density averaged over the distribution of fitness effects `μ`: `∫ φ_σ(x) dμ(σ)`.

results.title: Integrability of the expected spectrum in the selection coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `1 ≤ i < n`, the expected spectrum `E ξ_i(σ)` is integrable in `σ` against every finite measure.

results.title: Mixture identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite measure `μ` of selection coefficients and a segregating class `1 ≤ i < n`, the DFE-averaged spectrum is the binomial sampling integral of the DFE-averaged frequency density: `∫ E ξ_i(σ) dμ(σ) = ∫₀¹ C(n, i) x ^ i (1 - x) ^ (n - i) (∫ φ_σ(x) dμ(σ)) dx`.

results.title: Spectrum under a point-mass DFE is the single-selection spectrum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A DFE concentrated on one selection coefficient gives the single-`σ` spectrum.

results.title: DFE spectrum is additive in the measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The spectrum is additive in the (finite) DFE.

results.title: DFE spectrum is homogeneous in the measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The spectrum is homogeneous in the DFE.

results.title: Gamma distribution of fitness effects
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The gamma distribution of fitness effects (Boyko et al. 2008): the scaled selection coefficient is `σ = -T` with `T ~ Gamma(a, r)`, shape `a > 0` and rate `r > 0` (scale `1 / r`), so new mutations are deleterious with mean strength `a / r`.

results.title: Gamma DFE is a probability measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The gamma DFE is a probability law.

results.title: No mutation is beneficial under the gamma DFE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the gamma DFE no mutation is beneficial.

results.title: Mean selection coefficient under the gamma DFE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mean scaled selection coefficient under the gamma DFE is `-a / r`.

results.title: Variance of the selection coefficient under the gamma DFE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The variance of the scaled selection coefficient under the gamma DFE is `a / r ^ 2`.

results.title: Rescaling a gamma DFE divides its rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Rescaling a gamma DFE by `c > 0` (for example from `s` to `σ = 2Ns`, `c = 2N`) keeps the shape and divides the rate by `c`.

results.title: Fraction of strongly deleterious mutations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the gamma DFE the fraction of new mutations with `σ < -c`, `c ≥ 0`, is the gamma tail `Γ(a, r c) / Γ(a)`.

results.title: Fraction of mutations in a strength interval under the gamma DFE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fraction of new mutations whose strength `-σ` lies in `(c₁, c₂]`, `0 ≤ c₁ ≤ c₂`, is `(Γ(a, r c₁) - Γ(a, r c₂)) / Γ(a)`.

results.title: Site-frequency spectrum under the gamma DFE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The spectrum under the gamma DFE as an integral against the gamma law of the strength.

results.title: Poisson log-likelihood of counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Poisson log-likelihood `∑ (k_i log E_i - E_i - log k_i!)` of counts `k_i` with means `E_i`. Meaningful for `E_i > 0`; at `E_i = 0` Lean's `log 0 = 0` gives a junk value.

results.title: Probability of a count vector under independent Poisson laws
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The joint law of independent Poisson counts with means `E_i` gives the count vector `k` the probability `∏ e^{-E_i} E_i ^ {k_i} / (k_i!)`.

results.title: The Poisson-random-field log-likelihood
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For independent Poisson counts with positive means `E_i`, the log-probability of the observed counts `k` is `poissonLogLik E k`.

results.title: Derivative of the Poisson log-likelihood
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The derivative of the log-likelihood in the parameter `ψ`, when the means `E_i(ψ)` are positive and differentiable at `ψ`: `∑ (k_i / E_i(ψ) - 1) · DE_i(ψ)`.

results.title: Score equations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `ψ` maximizes the Poisson log-likelihood over a parameter set `S` that is a neighborhood of `ψ`, and the means are positive and differentiable at `ψ`, then `∑ (k_i / E_i(ψ) - 1) · DE_i(ψ) = 0`.

results.title: Profile maximum in `θ`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With means `E_i = θ f_i` linear in the mutation parameter, positive `f_i` and at least one count, every `θ > 0` has likelihood at most that of `θ̂ = ∑ k_i / ∑ f_i`.

results.title: Exchangeable pair of statistics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The pair of statistics `(X, Y)` is exchangeable under `μ`: the joint law is unchanged by swapping the two coordinates. This is an additional calibration assumption for a two-group haplotype test, stronger than the ordinary neutral null. Defined as `IdentDistrib` of the two orderings, so the measurability of the joint laws is part of the hypothesis rather than restored separately in each theorem.

results.title: Exchangeability is preserved by a common measurable map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Applying the same measurable function to both statistics preserves exchangeability.

results.title: Difference of an exchangeable pair has a symmetric law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The difference of an exchangeable pair has a symmetric law.

results.title: Equal tails of the difference of an exchangeable pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Equal tails: the upper tail of `X - Y` at `t` has the same probability as the lower tail at `-t`.

results.title: Two-sided rejection region splits into equal tails
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A two-sided rejection region splits into two tails of equal probability.

results.title: Equal tails of the log ratio of an exchangeable pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For positive statistics, the log ratio — the XP-EHH form — has equal tails.

results.title: Equal tails of the ratio of an exchangeable pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The same statement for the ratio itself, the form used for relative EHH: the probability that the ratio exceeds `c` equals the probability that it falls below `1 / c`.

results.title: Cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity (XP-EHH)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity score (Sabeti et al. 2007): the log ratio of the integrated haplotype homozygosities of the same core region in two populations. Both arguments must be positive for the score to be meaningful. Outside that domain `Real.log` is totalized by Mathlib, not by the stated junk value: `Real.log 0 = 0` and `Real.log (-x) = Real.log x`, so for example…

results.title: XP-EHH in star-genealogy sweep models
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: XP-EHH computed from two star-genealogy sweep models with the same recombination rate is the log ratio of the two ages, with the opposite sign to `ihs`.

results.title: Symmetry of the XP-EHH law under exchangeability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under exchangeability, the XP-EHH score has a symmetric law: the two tails of the two-sided test carry the same probability.
